Is AliExpress a Scam? UK Guide to Marketplace Risk

AliExpress is an Alibaba Group retail marketplace; that does not make every third-party listing genuine or every purchase protected in the same way.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-04-21 · Updated 2026-07-10 · 2 min read

AliExpress scamAliExpress fake sellersAliExpress scam UKAliExpress counterfeitAliExpress non-delivery scamfake website UKscam website UK
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Report it — call Action Fraud on 0300 123 2040 (Police Scotland: 101), and forward scam texts to 7726.
On this page

  2. Warning signs

What is verified about the platform

Alibaba Group says AliExpress launched in 2010 as a global retail e-commerce platform that connects consumers with manufacturers and merchants. It is therefore inaccurate to describe the whole platform as a fabricated site.

Buyers can still encounter goods that do not arrive, do not match the listing, are unsafe or infringe intellectual-property rights. Assess the individual seller, listing and protection terms.

Warning signs

  • A price that is implausibly low for the claimed brand or specification.
  • A seller with little history or reviews that do not discuss the actual product.
  • Stock images with no useful buyer evidence.
  • A request to pay, communicate or accept a refund outside AliExpress.
  • Pressure to confirm receipt before inspection.

Buyer Protection and Free Return are not one universal promise

The original draft said Buyer Protection universally covered a buyer for 15 days “from confirming receipt” for non-delivery, damage or misdescription. The official terms reviewed do not support that simplified statement for every UK order.

AliExpress does publish a 15-calendar-day Free Return term for participating products carrying the Free Return label. That is a particular programme with eligibility and return-condition rules, not proof that every dispute has the same deadline.

For a problem, open the order in the AliExpress account and use the dispute or return control before the deadline displayed there. Save screenshots of the listing, seller messages, tracking and the condition of the item.

The original “refunds typically take 1–10 working days” claim was also removed because no current universal UK term supporting it was found.

UK card protection

Chargeback may apply under card-scheme rules, commonly with a time limit around 120 days. Section 75 may apply to a qualifying credit-card purchase where the cash price is over £100 and not more than £30,000, but a marketplace or payment intermediary can affect the required debtor-creditor-supplier relationship. Ask the issuer to assess the claim.

Reporting

Use the order’s dispute process and AliExpress Help Centre. If the issue is fraud and money was lost, report at reportfraud.police.uk or on 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland; in Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101. Unsafe products can also be reported to Citizens Advice for referral to Trading Standards.

Frequently asked questions

Is AliExpress owned by Alibaba Group?

Yes. Alibaba Group identifies AliExpress as one of its e-commerce businesses.

Does every AliExpress order have the same 15-day protection window?

No universal rule was verified. Fifteen days is expressly used for eligible Free Return products, while other dispute rights and deadlines should be checked on the specific order.

Is section 75 automatic on AliExpress?

No. The cash-price and credit requirements matter, and the marketplace/payment structure may affect the claim.
